title.narrative: Growing Solaris to for bio-fuel production with the Bafokeng people in South Africa

description.narrative: Being mainly a mining area, there currently is little agricultural activity in the Royal Bafokeng Nation (RBN) and South Africa struggles with an unemployment rate above 25%. In the RBN’s Masterplan ‘a vision for 2035’ the region is determined to diversify its agricultural activities and aims to make its mining operations greener, for which Solaris may offer a solution. Solaris is a high yielding oil seed crop with excellent co-products such as high protein cake and biomass which can be used for animal feed and biofuel production. The Solaris oil extracted from the seed was used to power Africa’s first green flights between Johannesburg and Cape Town, operated by South African Airways. Sunchem BV, the owner of the seeds and plants of the Solaris variety, and its local partner Moumo are now looking to expand Solaris growing activities in the RBN in South Africa in order to make the South African Aviation sector more sustainable. To ensure the Solaris crop can be grown in the area and to prepare for future investments, Technical Assistance provided support. The project included the set-up of a local Solaris nursery, 3 trial locations for Solaris seed cultivation to test the best soil and seeds for high yield harvesting and other applications of the crops and the development of a bankable business plan. The project supported 8 direct jobs, 23 indirect jobs, led to knowledge transfer by training 3 farmers regarding Solaris cultivation through intercropping and the development of cultivation guidelines for future Solaris farmers. The pilot was successful and further partnerships and investments are being prepared as this is the first fully sustainable, circular and RSB certified project in South Africa. An MOU with key stakeholders in the South African Aviation sector for the production and use of green jet fuels using Solaris has been signed. This is likely to result in investments in the upscaling of the Solaris nursery, 5,000 ha of large scale Solaris cultivation with at least 300 local farming families and a processing facility for bio fuels and other applications. This new supply chain for biofuels is expected to create at least 4,000 direct and indirect jobs within the next 5 years.
